subjective.topic: Cyber Law Basics & Categories of Cyber Crime
subjective.question: What is cyber law?
subjective.answer: The term "Cyber Law" refers to all the legal and regulatory aspects of the Internet and its users. It is the body of law that deals with the legal issues arising from the use of computers, networks and the Internet — such as e-commerce, electronic contracts and signatures, cyber crime, privacy, and intellectual property in cyberspace.

subjective.topic: Cyber Law Basics & Categories of Cyber Crime
subjective.question: What is the difference between cyber crime against individual and cyber crime against property?
subjective.answer: Cyber crime is divided into three categories: cyber crime against the individual, against property, and against the government. A cyber crime against an individual is directed at a person — for example cyber stalking, cyber bullying, harassment, defamation, or stealing a person's identity through electronic communication. A cyber crime against property is directed at a person's property or data — for example, stealing a person's bank details and misusing the credit card to make purchases online, or damaging and destroying data (cyber vandalism).

subjective.topic: Cyber Law Basics & Categories of Cyber Crime
subjective.question: Difference between cyber crime against government and individual.
subjective.answer: Cyber crime against the government is referred to as cyber terrorism: in this category criminals hack military or government websites or circulate propaganda against the state. Cyber crime against an individual is directed at a single person rather than the state — for example cyber stalking, harassment, cyber bullying or identity theft committed against that person through electronic communication.

subjective.topic: Cyber Offences & Punishments — Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII of 2007 (Electronic Crime Bill 2007)
subjective.question: How many cyber offences defined in Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII or 2007?
subjective.answer: There are about 19 cyber offences defined in Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII of 2007, which was made to make provision for the prevention of electronic / cyber crimes.

subjective.topic: Cyber Offences & Punishments — Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII of 2007 (Electronic Crime Bill 2007)
subjective.question: Write down five offences defined in Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII or 2007?
subjective.answer: Five offences defined in the Ordinance are: (1) Criminal Access, (2) Criminal Data Access, (3) Data Damage, (4) System Damage, and (5) Electronic Fraud. Other offences defined in the same Ordinance include Electronic Forgery, Cyber Stalking, Spamming, Spoofing, Malicious Code, Misuse of Encryption, Unauthorized Access to Code, and Cyber Terrorism.

subjective.topic: Cyber Offences & Punishments — Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII of 2007 (Electronic Crime Bill 2007)
subjective.question: Data Destroying Penalty And Punishment
subjective.answer: Destroying or damaging data is the offence of Data Damage under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007, and its punishment is imprisonment for 3 years along with a fine of Rs. 3 Lac. Similarly, damaging an information system — altering, modifying, deleting or removing information, or creating hindrance in information access, knowingly and without authorization — is punishable with imprisonment for 7 years and a fine of Rs. 1 million.

subjective.topic: Cyber Offences & Punishments — Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXII of 2007 (Electronic Crime Bill 2007)
subjective.question: First Crime Bill Was introduced in
subjective.answer: The first cyber crime bill of Pakistan was the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Ordinance, promulgated by the President of Pakistan on 31st December 2007 (Ordinance No. LXXII of 2007); it is also referred to as the Prevention of Electronic Crime Ordinance 2008.

subjective.question: ETO 2002
subjective.answer: The Electronic Transactions Ordinance (ETO) 2002 was the first IT-relevant legislation created by national lawmakers in Pakistan. It has 43 sections and deals with the following 8 main areas relating to e-commerce: (1) Recognition of Electronic Documents, (2) Electronic Communications, (3) Web Site, (4) Digital Signatures Certification Providers, (5) Stamp Duty, (6) Attestation, certified copies, (7) Jurisdiction, and (8) Offences. Before ETO 2002 there was no legal recognition of electronic documentation, electronic records or digital signatures; after it, electronic documents and records were recognized, electronic and digital forms of authentication and identification were accepted, and messages through email, fax, mobile phones and plastic cards got legal recognition — giving protection to Pakistani e-commerce locally and globally.

subjective.question: Jurisdiction
subjective.answer: Jurisdiction is the right, power, or authority to administer justice by hearing and determining controversies (disputes). Its main types are territorial jurisdiction, extra-territorial jurisdiction and cyber jurisdiction. In cyberspace the question of jurisdiction is difficult because the Internet crosses national borders, so more than one country's courts may claim the power to hear the same case.

subjective.question: Types of jurisdiction, only names
subjective.answer: The types of jurisdiction are: (1) Territorial Jurisdiction, (2) Extra-Territorial Jurisdiction, and (3) Cyber Jurisdiction. (The course also discusses international jurisdiction for disputes that have an international dimension.)

subjective.question: What is license?
subjective.answer: A license is the description given by the owner (of a property or work) on how to use the property — that is, the permission granted by the owner allowing another person to use the property or work on the stated terms and conditions. In the same sense, the course notes describe a patent as a government authority or license conferring a right or title for a set period.

subjective.question: What is copyright and how it works? And write three examples of copyright?
subjective.answer: Copyright is the provision to own a work over a specific period of time: the creator or owner of an original work holds the rights over that work for a fixed period, so others cannot copy or use it freely; they may use it only as permitted, for example under the fair use clause, or under a license, which is the description given by the owner on how to use the property. Three examples of copyright works are: (1) books, (2) music, and (3) research journals. (Websites are also listed as copyright works in the course notes.)

subjective.question: List two Responsibilities of national cyber security forum?
subjective.answer: The Government is to create a National Cyber Security Forum and designate a lead ministry / agency for it. Two of its responsibilities are: (1) the lead ministry will publish a national calendar for holding cyber security seminars and organize national cyber security drills more than once annually; and (2) the lead ministry will run courses for parents to digitally monitor their children. (Under the same forum, universities are to group together to promote cyber security education under the umbrella of the HEC.)

subjective.question: What is a citizen's obligation?
subjective.answer: A citizen's digital right is to access all kinds of websites. A citizen's obligations in cyberspace are to prevent cyber bullying and sexual harassment, and to report illegal activity in cyberspace.

subjective.question: What is the analysis of cyber law situation in Pakistan?
subjective.answer: Overall, the situation of cyber laws is very encouraging in Pakistan, and Pakistan is ahead of many developing countries in this respect. The analysis of the above laws shows that: (1) there should be a well-coordinated effort to critically review the drafts already prepared; and (2) drafts of the remaining required laws should be prepared with a single focal point in the Federal Government, to avoid conflicts, overlapping and gaps.

subjective.question: Write down 5 GTLs ?
subjective.answer: "GTLs" here means gTLDs. A gTLD is a generic top-level domain — the top-level domain of an Internet address. Five gTLDs are: .com, .net, .org, .biz and .info. (The seven new gTLDs selected by ICANN on November 16, 2000 were: .aero, .biz, .coop, .info, .museum, .name and .pro.)

subjective.question: Pure E Commerce
subjective.answer: In pure e-commerce, all the dimensions are digital in nature — the product or service, the process, and the delivery agent are all digital (for example, buying and downloading software or an e-book entirely online). This is the opposite of traditional e-commerce, in which all the dimensions are physical in nature.

subjective.question: Give two website names which people can add comments, share videos, comments.
subjective.answer: Two such websites are Facebook and YouTube — social networking / sharing websites on which people can add comments and share videos, photos and comments with others. (The course notes name Facebook, MySpace and Twitter as social networking sites which provide links to many friends to maintain their relationships.)

subjective.question: Effects of Cyber Culture on Society
subjective.answer: Cyber culture is indicated to break down borders and barriers, not only between nations but also between groups and individuals, and it has reduced the gap between groups and individuals separated from each other. It has brought a great impact on an individual's life: in education, the style of teaching and learning has changed and student–teacher interactivity can be formed online, and it has great influence in the business world. On the negative side, those who are cut off from cyber culture feel more isolated from society and are not properly updated about the latest developments, and face-to-face communication is becoming weak due to the emerging social networks. Overall, a new uniform global culture is developing.

subjective.question: Cyber security
subjective.answer: Cyber security refers to the technologies and processes designed to protect computers, networks and data from unauthorized access and attacks delivered through the Internet by cyber criminals. Security deals with three primary issues, called the CIA triad: confidentiality, integrity and availability.

subjective.question: Cryptography
subjective.answer: Cryptography is the science/method of protecting information by converting it into an unreadable form so that only authorized persons can understand it. The method of hiding plaintext in such a way as to hide its substance is called encryption, and encrypting plaintext results in unreadable gibberish called cipher text, which the receiver converts back into plaintext using the key. Public key cryptography is also known as asymmetric cryptography.

subjective.question: Certificate Manager and distribution
subjective.answer: Certificate management and distribution is a part of the Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). A Certification Authority, or CA, is authorized to issue (digital) certificates to its computer users; a CA's role is analogous to a country's government's Passport Office — it verifies the identity of the user and issues a certificate that binds the user to his/her public key. These certificates are then distributed so that other people can verify the identity and digital signatures of the certificate holder.

subjective.question: What is cyber crime? How can a computer be used as a weapon for crime and as a target of crime?
subjective.answer: One of the largest computer security companies, Symantec Corporation, defines cybercrime as "any crime that is committed using a computer or network, or hardware device". A computer may be used as a weapon for crime — for example, sending malicious code, spamming or committing electronic fraud through it — or it may itself be the target of crime, as in criminal access, data damage or damage to an information system.

subjective.question: Define hacking and cyber vandalism.
subjective.answer: Hacking, in simple terms, means illegal access into a computer system without the permission of the computer owner/user. Damaging or destroying data rather than stealing or misusing them is called cyber vandalism.

subjective.question: What is identity theft? What is software piracy?
subjective.answer: Identity theft is the crime in which a criminal accesses data about a person's bank account, credit cards, debit card and other sensitive information and misuses that person's identity. Software piracy is the crime in which a person violates copyrights and does unauthorized copying of software.

subjective.topic: Offences & Punishments under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007
subjective.question: What is cyber stalking? State its punishment under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007.
subjective.answer: Whoever, with intent to harass any person, uses a computer, computer network, the Internet or any similar means of communication to communicate obscene, vulgar, profane, lewd, lascivious or indecent language, picture or image, threatens any illegal or immoral act, or takes or distributes pictures or photographs of any person without his knowledge, commits the offence of cyber stalking. Its punishment is imprisonment for 3 years and a fine of Rs. 3 Lac.

subjective.topic: Offences & Punishments under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007
subjective.question: Differentiate between spamming and spoofing, and state the punishment of each.
subjective.answer: Spamming means sending illegal electronic messages to any person without the permission of the recipient; its punishment is imprisonment for 6 months and a fine of Rs. 50,000. Spoofing means establishing a website, or sending an electronic message with a fake source intended to be believed by the recipient to be an authentic source, with intent to gain unauthorized access or obtain valuable information; its punishment is imprisonment for 3 years and a fine of Rs. 3 Lac.

subjective.topic: Offences & Punishments under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007
subjective.question: What is electronic forgery? State its punishment.
subjective.answer: Whoever, for unlawful gain, interferes with data, an electronic system or a device, with intent to cause harm or to commit fraud by any input, alteration, or suppression of data, resulting in unauthentic data that is considered or acted upon for legal purposes as if it were authentic, commits electronic forgery. Its punishment is imprisonment for 7 years and a fine of Rs. 7 Lac.

subjective.topic: Offences & Punishments under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007
subjective.question: What is cyber terrorism? State its punishment under the Electronic Crime Bill 2007.
subjective.answer: Crimes against a government are referred to as cyber terrorism — for example, hacking military websites or circulating propaganda. Under the punishment table of the Electronic Crime Bill 2007, cyber terrorism is punishable with life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 10 Million.

subjective.question: Write any five responsibilities of the National Response Centre for Cyber Crimes (NR3C).
subjective.answer: Five responsibilities of the NR3C are: (1) to enhance the capability of the Government of Pakistan and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to effectively prevent growing cyber crimes; (2) it is the reporting and investigation centre for all types of cyber crimes in the country; (3) liaison with all relevant national and international organizations to handle cases against cyber criminals; (4) to provide necessary technical support to all sensitive government organizations to make their critical information resources secure; and (5) to provide timely information to critical infrastructure owners and government departments about threats, actual attacks and recovery techniques — a role of a Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT). It also carries out R&D activities and provides electronic forensic services.

subjective.question: What powers does the Electronic Crime Bill 2007 give to the FIA?
subjective.answer: The Electronic Crime Bill 2007 gives exclusive powers to the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to investigate and charge cases against electronic crimes. The Bill applies to every person who commits an offence under it, irrespective of his nationality or citizenship.

subjective.question: Why do we need cyber law? (Need of cyber law)
subjective.answer: Trade and business communications through electronic means give rise to a number of legal issues. For instance, if a service is sold over the Internet across countries, in which geographical location can the transaction be deemed to have occurred? This question is important from the point of view of consumer protection and establishing jurisdiction. Furthermore, electronic transactions require electronic contracts and electronic signatures, which had not been provided for in the contract laws of many countries; most countries that wished to participate in electronic commerce therefore needed to undertake major legislative reforms. Cyber law is also needed to deal with regulatory issues, financial crimes, electronic forgery, cyber defamation, cyber stalking, intellectual property crimes, denial of service attacks and unauthorized access to computer systems.

subjective.question: What is a patent?
subjective.answer: A patent is a government authority or license conferring a right or title for a set period, especially the sole right to exclude others from making, using, or selling an invention. In Pakistan, patents are granted by the IPO (Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan) under the Patent Ordinance and Patent Rules.

subjective.question: What is cyber squatting?
subjective.answer: Cyber squatting is the behaviour of acquiring a domain name with the intention of reselling it to a third party which has a higher perceived value for that name, or to exploit the 'traffic' that the domain name generates based on consumers' presumption of the purpose of the domain name. In the cyber world, URLs are more like trademarks, so this practice abuses the trademark rights of businesses.

subjective.question: Differentiate between a gTLD and a ccTLD.
subjective.answer: A gTLD is a generic top-level domain — the top-level domain of an Internet address, for example .com, .NET and .org. A ccTLD is a country code top-level domain, for example .mx for Mexico (and .pk for Pakistan); ccTLDs are administered independently by nationally designated registration authorities, and there are 252 ccTLDs reflected in the database of the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA).

subjective.question: What is the CIA triad in cyber security?
subjective.answer: Security deals with three primary issues, called the CIA triad: Confidentiality (data is accessible only to authorized persons), Integrity (data is not altered improperly), and Availability (systems and data are available when needed).

subjective.question: Define encryption and cipher text.
subjective.answer: The method of hiding plaintext in such a way as to hide its substance is called encryption. Encrypting plaintext results in unreadable gibberish called cipher text, which can be converted back into the original plaintext only with the proper key.

subjective.question: What is key management in cryptography? Why is the safe delivery of the key important?
subjective.answer: In key management, both ends must agree upon a key and keep it secret between them. Being at different physical locations, they must trust a courier (a secure communication medium) to prevent the disclosure of the secret key, because anyone who overhears or intercepts the key in transit can later read, modify, and forge all information encrypted or authenticated with that key.

subjective.question: What is malware? Give one example.
subjective.answer: Malware is any software that infects and damages a computer system without the owner's knowledge or permission. An example is a Trojan horse — an email virus that can duplicate itself, steal information, or harm the computer system.

subjective.question: Write down the seven components of cyber culture.
subjective.answer: The seven components of cyber culture are: (1) Internet, (2) Website, (3) E-Mail, (4) Blog, (5) Online Chat, (6) E-Commerce, and (7) Social Networks.

subjective.question: Explain the B2B, B2C and C2B models of e-commerce.
subjective.answer: The B2B model describes commerce transactions between businesses, such as between a manufacturer and a wholesaler, or between a wholesaler and a retailer. The B2C model involves transactions between business organizations and consumers. The C2B model is a type of commerce where a consumer or end user provides a product or service to an organization.
